abstract: We exhibit examples of K-stable Fano varieties with obstructed qG-deformations; more precisely, their miniversal qG-deformation spaces can be non-reduced. As a consequence, we show that both the K-moduli stack and the K-moduli space can be non-reduced, and hence non-smooth, at points corresponding to K-stable Fano varieties.
hook: Some Fano varieties are K-stable yet cannot be deformed smoothly, so their moduli space is non-reduced.
hook_turn: so their moduli space is non-reduced.
summary: The authors build explicit examples of K-stable Fano varieties whose space of qG-deformations is non-reduced, meaning it carries hidden extra structure. This shows the K-moduli stack and space can be non-reduced, and so non-smooth, at points of K-stable varieties. The finding comes from specific examples, so it does not say how common the behavior is.
title: K-stable Fano varieties can have obstructed deformations
